correctness.rationale: The characteristic flag is preserved under all scalar extensions. Orthogonality kills every strict upper-triangular nonterminal image coefficient; the remaining diagonal powers and terminal-coordinate recursion give exactly a unit parameter constrained by the weight gcd and one free annihilator translation. Bezout gives the group scheme over arbitrary commutative base rings. The tangent equation \(gh=0\) proves the characteristic criterion; the order of 2 modulo p yields the sharp dimension cutoff. Independent derivation-equation row reduction, exhaustive binary four-by-four maps and explicit dual-number substitution checks all passed.

originality.rationale: Theorem 5.2 of Mukhamedov et al. (2018/2019) supplies ordinary automorphism matrices and the very same gcd condition in characteristic zero; it is explicitly credited and not asserted as new. Casas et al. (2012) classify/characterize the underlying maximal-index evolution algebras over complex coefficients, not automorphism group schemes. The currently checked sources and indexed findings do not yield functorial characteristic-p group schemes, nonreduced infinitesimal symmetries or the sharp modular dimension threshold. This is provisional historical priority, not an absolute novelty certificate.
residual_risks: An unlocated characteristic-p automorphism group-scheme paper may contain an equivalent or stronger theorem.

The 2018/2019 automorphism matrix constraints almost directly suggest the group-scheme presentation; their already established ordinary-point part is not claimed new, and the novelty distinction rests on the functorial modular, infinitesimal and sharp threshold statements.

value.rationale: The exact scheme-theoretic symmetry and smoothness boundary are natural invariants for an infinite family of maximal-nilindex nonassociative algebras. The parameter g encodes torsion invisible to ordinary finite-field automorphism cardinalities; the characteristic-two universal nonsmoothness and sharp odd-p first occurrence explain why characteristic-zero derivation classifications cannot be transferred by ordinary-point substitution. The result gives a concrete infinite family of hidden infinitesimal symmetries and a full structural description.
